label: First copy step after <DEL> (re-input of orig token 0) in long sequences, favoring i/d/m/w/l/o/0/a
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original inputs or the <DEL> step. 89% of activation mass is at recall_idx 1 (step L+1, where the input is the fed-back original token 0 and the output is original token 1); most of the rest is at recall_idx 2. Two things set the magnitude together, in a graded way: sequence length (rate at recall_idx 1 rises steeply with L, and 65% of mass comes from L=9; it essentially never fires for L<=5) and the identity of the first token (i and d give the strongest activations, all near max, then m, w, l, o, 0, a). It does not fire at recall_idx 0 or 3+, on first occurrences of a token, or in short sequences. A binary predicate cannot capture this cleanly: short sequences with i/d still fire weakly, and long sequences with other first tokens fire at low magnitude, so precision and recall both stay near 0.5-0.6. (recall_idx == 1) alone covers 89% of the mass, but with only 10% precision.
